mstts:express-as.prosody: Have you ever noticed how a single, nagging thought can echo in your mind—making you question if you really belong or if you’ve said the right thing? That quiet hum of self-doubt and the pressure of social anxiety? It can shape almost every moment, sometimes holding us back from showing up as our true selves. Together, we're about to explore how those inner critics work, and more importantly, how we can start to gently turn down their volume. In Ellen Hendriksen’s How to Be Yourself: Quiet Your Inner Critic and Rise Above Social Anxiety, she invites us to look at that dance between wanting to connect and feeling held back by insecurity. It’s not about chasing some perfect version of ourselves, but about learning how to treat ourselves with a little more kindness and understanding—especially on the days when we need it most. If you’ve ever felt your heart race before speaking up, hesitated to make eye contact, or worried about how you’re coming across in a group, you’re not alone. Hendriksen shares real stories and science-backed strategies that help us face these moments, not by trying to erase anxiety altogether, but by learning to move with it—building our confidence one step at a time. So, as we begin this journey together, let’s get curious about what it means to be truly ourselves. Imagine stepping into social situations with more ease and honesty, and finding deeper, more meaningful connections along the way. Ready to discover how that’s possible? Let’s dive in.
